correctness.rationale: The universal rooted upper bound is not inferred from finite data: positive response to a size-k cluster exactly factors into laminar hierarchies of sizes k and n-k+1. Disjoint-alphabet product Littlestone dimensions add, so its depth is n-3 inductively, excluding depth n-1. Binary-prefix grafting shatters n-2 queries and containment transfers upper bound. Outgroup-rooting gives exact unrooted split equivalence. Definitions include proper clades, n=2 base, n=3 unrooted base; packaged standalone finite checker passes against the theorem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The triplet-query online dimension compares order relationships within labeled triples; here a single query asks whether an arbitrary k-subset is EXACTLY a proper cluster. The latter exact linear formula neither follows from the former multiclass theorem nor from hierarchy refinement metrics.

value.rationale: Determines a natural entire-family (not arbitrary small slice) exact static and adaptive invariant for binary and nonbinary rooted trees and their unrooted split counterparts. Product factorization gives structural insight into a sharp linear online depth despite (2n-3)!! hypotheses, and formalizes a meaningful query-language contrast with published multiclass triple-labeled tree learning. Does not assert a full sample-complexity result.
